articles.title: JNTUH warns staff against corruption, bribery
articles.description:
HYDERABAD: Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH) has warned its teaching and non-teaching staff against corruption, unauthorised financial transactions and fraudulent practices, saying strict disciplinary action, including suspension and dismissal from service, will be taken against those found guilty. Registrar issues warning against unethical practices In a circular issued on July 20, JNTUH Registrar Dr [...]HYDERABAD: Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH) has warned its teaching and non-teaching staff against corruption, unauthorised financial transactions and fraudulent practices, saying strict disciplinary action, including suspension and dismissal from service, will be taken against those found guilty.

Registrar issues warning against unethical practices

In a circular issued on July 20, JNTUH Registrar Dr A. Jaya Laxmi said the university had received information that some employees were violating rules, engaging in unauthorised transactions and accepting bribes from vendors in return for favours. The circular also stated that some staff members were allegedly collecting money from colleagues.

"Corruption, illegal activities and fraudulent practices will not be tolerated. Any employee found indulging in such activities will face suspension and removal from service. Every employee must discharge duties with ethical standards, transparency and accountability," the Registrar said.

Circular follows allegations over university operations

JNTUH is among the country's prominent technological universities and has around 250 affiliated private engineering, pharmacy and management colleges. The university oversees inspections, affiliation, seat approvals, additional intake permissions and examination-related processes. It also manages constituent campuses at Rajanna Sircilla, Wanaparthy, Palair and Mahabubabad.

The university's expanding administrative responsibilities, including tenders, procurement and infrastructure works, have led to recurring allegations that some teaching and non-teaching staff were misusing these processes for personal gain. Allegations have also surfaced that a few faculty members amassed substantial wealth through corrupt practices.

University sources said these issues prompted the Registrar to issue the written warning. While reports of corruption at JNTUH have appeared in the media in the past, the latest circular is being viewed as the university's first formal acknowledgement of concerns over unethical practices.

When contacted, the Registrar said no specific cases of corruption or irregularities had been officially established. However, she said the circular was intended to caution employees against engaging in such activities. She added that the circular had been circulated to all departments and employees' signatures had been obtained after its communication.

Allegations highlighted in the report

Among the allegations cited are demands for ₹4 lakh from some private colleges during the affiliation process. A senior professor who was part of an inspection team allegedly sought the money, with college managements reportedly paying to avoid reductions in sanctioned seats.

The report also alleges that faculty ratification, promotions in private colleges and postgraduate project viva examinations were turned into sources of illegal income.

Separate allegations relate to university engineering works, with claims that hostel mess contracts were awarded only after payments were made to certain officials. Audio recordings purportedly featuring an official discussing such arrangements with a contractor reportedly surfaced recently.

In another instance, a contractor was initially declared ineligible for a college building project before the tender was cancelled and reissued, after which the same contractor secured the work.

The report further alleges that, in a recent procurement of laboratory equipment through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal, the lowest bidder was later disqualified after the tender process was reopened. ]]>

articles.title: Major Ravi served legal notice for defamatory remarks towards protestors at Jantar Mantar
articles.description: KOCHI: A legal notice has been served to Major Ravi for his defamatory remarks towards the protestors in Jantar Mantar. The notice was sent by Malavika, a plus two student. The notice has demanded to tender an apology after withdrawing the remarks within seven days of receiving the notice and also asked him to remove the video from the social media.

articles.title: GHMC plans Mylardevpally-Katedan flyover
articles.description:
HYDERABAD: The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) has proposed another major flyover project to provide long-term relief from traffic congestion in the Old City. The civic body submitted a proposal to the state government about six months ago for the construction of a six-lane grade separator linking Mylardevpally, Katedan Junction and the Shamshabad road. The [...]HYDERABAD: The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) has proposed another major flyover project to provide long-term relief from traffic congestion in the Old City. The civic body submitted a proposal to the state government about six months ago for the construction of a six-lane grade separator linking Mylardevpally, Katedan Junction and the Shamshabad road. The project is currently awaiting administrative approval.

Six-lane corridor to improve airport connectivity

The proposed grade separator will be built over 2.08 km at an estimated cost of ₹345 crore. It has been planned to address traffic bottlenecks at Katedan Junction, one of Hyderabad's busiest intersections.

Once completed, the corridor is expected to improve connectivity from the Old City as well as LB Nagar, Uppal and Karmanghat to Shamshabad via Mylardevpally and Katedan. The project is expected to provide faster access to the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport for commuters.

Work to begin after approvals

GHMC officials said the tender process will begin after the project receives administrative approval from the state government, following which construction work will commence.

articles.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Rollout Begins in West Bengal Following State Committee Formation
articles.description: PM Vishwakarma Scheme Rollout Begins in West Bengal Following State Committee Formation New Delhi, Jul 24 (KNN) The Ministry of MSME has begun implementing the PM Vishwakarma Scheme in West Bengal following the constitution of the State Monitoring Committee and District Implementation Committees by the West Bengal Government on May 14, 2026. The information was provided by Union Minister of State for MSME Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. PM Vishwakarma was launched on September 17, 2023, to provide end-to-end support to artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades, including carpentry, pottery, goldsmithing, tailoring, masonry and fishing net making. Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), 5.82 crore loans amounting to Rs 3.55 lakh crore have been disbursed in West Bengal from April 8, 2015, to June 26, 2026. The Ministry has also stated that 23 Host Institutes are operating in West Bengal under the Incubation Component of the MSME Innovative Scheme. Each approved idea is eligible for financial support of up to Rs 15 lakh. Women entrepreneurs, including those based in the Sundarbans, are eligible for support under various schemes, including Udyam Registration, the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, CGTMSE, PMEGP, PM Vishwakarma, the Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme and the Yashasvini Campaign. (KNN Bureau)

articles.title: PM Vishwakarma and PMMY Boost MSMEs in West Bengal
articles.description: PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched on 17.09.2023 to provide end-to-end holistic support to artisans and craftspeople of 18 traditional trades who work with their hands and tools. The scheme covers 18 trades, namely Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal Artisan, Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Footwear Artisan, Mason, Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor and Fishing Net Maker. The implementation of PM Vishwakarma has commenced in the State of West Bengal following the issuance of a notification by the Government of West Bengal constituting the State Monitoring Committee and District Implementation Committees on 14.05.2026 for the roll-out of the Scheme in the State. Under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), a total of 5.82 crore loans amounting to Rs. 3.55 lakh crore have been disbursed since inception i.e. 08.04.2015 till 26.06.2026 in the State of West Bengal. The Government has undertaken the following initiatives for potential women beneficiaries throughout the country including Sundarbans-based women entrepreneurs and fisherfolk: Udyam Registration Portal (UR) and Udyam Assist Portal (UAP): women owned enterprises registered are eligible to avail benefits under various schemes of the Ministry including access to Priority Sector Lending. Public Procurement Policy for MSEs: Central Ministries and CPSEs are mandated to procure atleast 3% of their annual procurement from women owned Micro and Small Enterprises, thereby facilitating market access. Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE): women owned Micro and Small Enterprises are eligible for enhanced guarantee coverage of upto 90% (as against 75% for others) and a 10% concession in the annual guarantee fee. PMEGP: Women beneficiaries are categorized under Special Category and eligible for a higher Margin Money (MM) Subsidy rate of upto 35% and lower own contribution of 5% of project cost, compared to 25% MM Subsidy rate and 10% own contribution of project cost for beneficiaries under General category. Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana: Women artisans engaged in the coir sector are provided with skill upgradation training under the Coir Vikas Yojana to enhance their employability and entrepreneurial capabilities. Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme: women entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance of upto 100% of the admissible expenditure for participation in domestic trade fairs, compared to 80% for other entrepreneurs. PM Vishwakarma Scheme: women artisans engaged in any of the 18 notified trades are eligible for benefits including skill training, toolkit incentive, collateral free credit support, incentive for digital transactions and marketing support. Yashasvini Campaign: Ministry undertakes awareness, handholding, mentorship and capacity building activities to facilitate access of existing and aspiring women entrepreneurs to various Government schemes and institutional support. The Incubation Component of the MSME Innovative Scheme of the Ministry of MSME is aimed at promoting innovation, support new ideas, and facilitate the transformation of concepts into viable business ventures. It plays a crucial role in strengthening the MSME and thus, start-up ecosystem by nurturing early-stage ideas. It supports the process of incubation through Host Institutes (HI), which are academic institutions and Innovation centers acting as Business Incubators (BI) across the country. Currently, there are 23 Host Institutes (HI) in West Bengal and each approved idea is eligible for financial support of up to a maximum amount of Rs. 15 lakh.
